title: Pride and Prejudice
author: Jane Austen
description: Elizabeth Bennet and the proud Mr Darcy misjudge each other across a series of balls, visits and proposals, in a comedy about money, manners and first impressions.

title: Emma
author: Jane Austen
description: A clever, comfortable young woman sets about arranging her neighbours' love lives in a small English village, and is wrong about nearly all of them, herself included.

title: Jane Eyre
author: Charlotte Brontë
description: An orphan who will not be talked down to becomes governess at Thornfield Hall, where her employer Mr Rochester keeps a secret on the top floor.

title: Wuthering Heights
author: Emily Brontë
description: On the Yorkshire moors, the foundling Heathcliff and Catherine Earnshaw form a bond so fierce that it ruins two families over two generations.

title: Great Expectations
author: Charles Dickens
description: Pip, a blacksmith's boy, is given money by an unknown benefactor to become a gentleman, and learns slowly what that is worth and who he owes it to.

title: A Tale of Two Cities
author: Charles Dickens
description: London and Paris before and during the French Revolution, following a family drawn back to France and the men who would give anything for them.

title: Middlemarch
author: George Eliot
description: Life in a provincial English town around 1830, through an idealistic young woman, an ambitious doctor and the marriages that test them both.

title: Moby-Dick
author: Herman Melville
description: Ishmael signs on to the whaler Pequod, whose captain means to hunt down the white whale that took his leg, whatever it costs the crew.

title: Frankenstein
subtitle: or, The Modern Prometheus
author: Mary Shelley
description: A young scientist builds a living being from the dead and abandons it, and the creature, educated and lonely, comes looking for an answer.

title: Dracula
author: Bram Stoker
description: Told in letters and diaries: a solicitor's visit to a Transylvanian count, and the count's arrival in England, where a small group sets out to stop him.

title: The Great Gatsby
author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
description: One summer on Long Island, Nick Carraway watches his neighbour Jay Gatsby throw lavish parties in the hope that Daisy Buchanan will walk into one.

title: Mrs Dalloway
author: Virginia Woolf
description: A single June day in London after the First World War, moving between a society hostess preparing a party and a shell-shocked veteran.

title: Nineteen Eighty-Four
author: George Orwell
description: Winston Smith rewrites history for the Party in a state that watches everyone, and begins, carefully, to keep a diary of his own.

title: Animal Farm
author: George Orwell
description: The animals drive out the farmer and promise equality for all; the pigs then rewrite the rules one commandment at a time.

title: Brave New World
author: Aldous Huxley
description: A future of engineered contentment, where people are bred for their place and kept happy with pleasure and drugs, is visited by a man raised outside it.

title: To Kill a Mockingbird
author: Harper Lee
description: In a small Alabama town in the 1930s, Scout Finch watches her father defend a Black man accused of a crime, and her neighbours' reactions to it.

title: The Catcher in the Rye
author: J. D. Salinger
description: Expelled from prep school, sixteen-year-old Holden Caulfield spends a few aimless days in New York, impatient with everyone he meets and unsure of himself.

title: Beloved
author: Toni Morrison
description: Years after escaping slavery, Sethe lives in a house in Ohio haunted by the daughter she lost, until a young woman arrives calling herself Beloved.

title: Song of Solomon
author: Toni Morrison
description: Milkman Dead leaves Michigan in search of family gold and finds instead the story of his ancestors, told through songs and names.

title: The Remains of the Day
author: Kazuo Ishiguro
description: An English butler takes a motoring trip in 1956 and looks back on decades of loyal service, and on what he did not let himself feel.

title: Never Let Me Go
author: Kazuo Ishiguro
description: Kathy remembers her school days at Hailsham, an English boarding school whose pupils were told, gently and incompletely, what their lives were for.

title: Klara and the Sun
author: Kazuo Ishiguro
description: An Artificial Friend watches from a shop window, then from a family's home, trying to understand the sick girl she has been bought to look after.

title: The Handmaid's Tale
author: Margaret Atwood
description: In the Republic of Gilead, Offred is assigned to bear children for a powerful household, and remembers, in secret, the life that was taken from her.

title: The Left Hand of Darkness
author: Ursula K. Le Guin
description: An envoy comes to the frozen planet Gethen, whose people have no fixed sex, and must learn to trust one of them on a long journey across the ice.

title: The Fellowship of the Ring
author: J. R. R. Tolkien
description: Frodo Baggins inherits a ring that its maker wants back, and sets out from the Shire with companions to carry it somewhere it can be destroyed.

title: Dune
author: Frank Herbert
description: On the desert planet Arrakis, the only source of a precious spice, a young duke's son survives his family's betrayal and is taken in by its desert people.

title: Foundation
author: Isaac Asimov
description: A mathematician predicts the fall of a galactic empire and sets up a colony of scholars to shorten the dark age that follows.

title: The Murder of Roger Ackroyd
author: Agatha Christie
description: Hercule Poirot, retired to a village to grow marrows, is drawn into the death of a wealthy widower, told by the local doctor.

title: And Then There Were None
author: Agatha Christie
description: Ten strangers invited to an island off the Devon coast are accused of past crimes by a gramophone record, and begin to die one by one.

title: The Big Sleep
author: Raymond Chandler
description: Private detective Philip Marlowe is hired by an old general over a blackmail note and finds himself in the middle of his daughters' troubles in Los Angeles.

title: The Talented Mr. Ripley
author: Patricia Highsmith
description: Tom Ripley is paid to bring a rich man's son home from Italy, and finds he would much rather have the son's life than go home himself.

title: Rebecca
author: Daphne du Maurier
description: A shy young bride arrives at Manderley, her husband's Cornish estate, and finds the memory of his first wife in every room.

title: Things Fall Apart
author: Chinua Achebe
description: Okonkwo, a proud wrestler and farmer in an Igbo village, sees his world change when missionaries and colonial officers arrive.

title: Their Eyes Were Watching God
author: Zora Neale Hurston
description: Janie Crawford tells a friend the story of her three marriages and her search, in all-Black towns in Florida, for a life that is her own.

title: Invisible Man
author: Ralph Ellison
description: A nameless young Black man moves from the South to Harlem, through college, a factory and a political movement, none of which really see him.

title: The Road
author: Cormac McCarthy
description: A father and his young son walk south through a burned, ash-covered America, carrying what they can and trying to stay good.

title: Wolf Hall
author: Hilary Mantel
description: Thomas Cromwell, a blacksmith's son, rises to become Henry VIII's most useful servant while the king seeks to end his first marriage.

title: Life of Pi
author: Yann Martel
description: After a shipwreck, a zookeeper's son from Pondicherry spends months in a lifeboat on the Pacific with a Bengal tiger.

title: Atonement
author: Ian McEwan
description: On a hot day in 1935 a thirteen-year-old girl misreads what she sees and makes an accusation that shapes three lives through the war that follows.

title: The Secret History
author: Donna Tartt
description: A student from California joins a small circle of classics students at a Vermont college, and tells how they came to kill one of their own.

title: Gone Girl
author: Gillian Flynn
description: On their fifth anniversary Amy Dunne disappears from her Missouri home, and the story is told in turns by her husband and by her diary.

title: The Silence of the Lambs
author: Thomas Harris
description: FBI trainee Clarice Starling seeks the help of an imprisoned psychiatrist and murderer to catch a killer who is still at large.

title: The Shining
author: Stephen King
description: A recovering alcoholic takes a winter caretaker's job at a remote Colorado hotel, with his wife and their son, who can see what the hotel wants.

title: The Martian
author: Andy Weir
description: Left for dead after a dust storm, an astronaut must make his supplies last on Mars until a rescue can reach him, solving one problem at a time.

title: Project Hail Mary
author: Andy Weir
description: A science teacher wakes alone on a spacecraft with no memory of why, and slowly works out that the Sun's fading depends on him.

title: Station Eleven
author: Emily St. John Mandel
description: Years after a flu pandemic, a travelling company performs Shakespeare to scattered settlements, linked to a famous actor who died the night it began.

title: The Underground Railroad
author: Colson Whitehead
description: Cora escapes a Georgia plantation on an underground railroad that here is a real train, travelling state by state through versions of America.

title: Normal People
author: Sally Rooney
description: Connell and Marianne, from the same small Irish town but different classes, drift together and apart through school and university in Dublin.

title: Americanah
author: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie
description: Ifemelu leaves Lagos to study in America and writes a blog about race there; years later she thinks of going home, and of the man she left.

title: A Gentleman in Moscow
author: Amor Towles
description: In 1922 a Russian count is sentenced to spend the rest of his life inside the Metropol hotel, and makes a full life within its walls.

title: Circe
author: Madeline Miller
description: The witch of the Odyssey tells her own story: daughter of the sun, exiled to an island, where she learns her craft and meets gods and heroes.

title: Where the Crawdads Sing
author: Delia Owens
description: Abandoned as a child in the North Carolina marshes, Kya grows up alone there, and years later is suspected when a local man is found dead.

title: Good Omens
author: Terry Pratchett and Neil Gaiman
description: An angel and a demon who have grown fond of life on Earth try to stop the end of the world, which keeps not going to plan.

title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
author: Douglas Adams
description: Minutes before Earth is demolished for a bypass, Arthur Dent is rescued by a friend who turns out to be from somewhere near Betelgeuse.

title: Dubliners
author: James Joyce
description: Fifteen stories of ordinary lives in Dublin at the turn of the twentieth century, ending with a long Christmas party and its aftermath.

title: Interpreter of Maladies
author: Jhumpa Lahiri
description: Nine stories about Indian and Indian-American lives, of couples, families and strangers, in Boston, Calcutta and places in between.

title: Leaves of Grass
author: Walt Whitman
description: Whitman's collection, which he kept revising and enlarging all his life, celebrating the body, democracy and the crowded variety of America.

title: Ariel
author: Sylvia Plath
description: Poems written in the last months of Plath's life and published after her death, among them Daddy, Lady Lazarus and the bee poems.

title: Maus
subtitle: A Survivor's Tale
author: Art Spiegelman
description: Spiegelman interviews his father about surviving Auschwitz, drawing Jews as mice and Nazis as cats, and records their difficult relationship along the way.

title: Persepolis
author: Marjane Satrapi
description: A black-and-white memoir in comics of a girlhood in Tehran during the Islamic Revolution and the war with Iraq.

title: Watchmen
author: Alan Moore
description: In an alternative 1985 where costumed heroes have been outlawed, the murder of one of them leads a former colleague to a larger plot.

title: Fun Home
subtitle: A Family Tragicomic
author: Alison Bechdel
description: A memoir in comics about growing up in a funeral home in Pennsylvania, and about a father whose secrets came out only after his death.

title: Cien años de soledad
author: Gabriel García Márquez
description: Seven generations of the Buendía family in the town of Macondo, where the miraculous is reported as plainly as the weather.

title: El amor en los tiempos del cólera
author: Gabriel García Márquez
description: Florentino Ariza waits more than fifty years for Fermina Daza, the woman who turned him down when they were young, in a Caribbean port city.

title: Don Quijote de la Mancha
author: Miguel de Cervantes
description: A country gentleman who has read too many tales of chivalry sets out as a knight errant with his practical squire, Sancho Panza.

title: La casa de los espíritus
author: Isabel Allende
description: Four generations of the Trueba family in an unnamed Latin American country, from the clairvoyant Clara to a granddaughter caught up in a coup.

title: Ficciones
author: Jorge Luis Borges
description: Short stories built like puzzles: an infinite library, a map as large as an empire's, a man who forgets nothing, a garden of forking paths.

title: L'Étranger
author: Albert Camus
description: Meursault, a clerk in Algiers, attends his mother's funeral without weeping, kills a man on a beach, and is tried as much for the first as the second.

title: Madame Bovary
author: Gustave Flaubert
description: Emma, married to a dull country doctor in Normandy, looks for the life she read about in novels, in affairs and in debts she cannot pay.

title: Les Misérables
author: Victor Hugo
description: The former convict Jean Valjean, pursued for decades by the policeman Javert, raises an orphan girl in Paris up to the barricades of 1832.

title: Die Verwandlung
author: Franz Kafka
description: Gregor Samsa, a travelling salesman, wakes one morning changed into an enormous insect, and his family must decide what to do with him.

title: Der Steppenwolf
author: Hermann Hesse
description: Harry Haller, a lonely intellectual who feels half man and half wolf, is led by a young woman into a world of jazz, dancing and a magic theatre.

title: L'amica geniale
author: Elena Ferrante
description: Elena and Lila grow up in a poor neighbourhood of Naples in the 1950s, rivals and best friends, one of them sent on to school and one not.

title: Il nome della rosa
author: Umberto Eco
description: In 1327 a Franciscan friar and his novice investigate deaths at an Italian abbey whose great library is closed to the monks themselves.

title: ノルウェイの森
author: Haruki Murakami
description: Hearing a Beatles song, Toru remembers his student years in Tokyo in the late 1960s, divided between two very different young women.

title: 人間失格
author: Osamu Dazai
description: The notebooks of a man who has never felt he understood other people, and who hides behind clowning until he can no longer.

title: Sapiens
subtitle: A Brief History of Humankind
author: Yuval Noah Harari
description: A sweeping account of how one species of human came to dominate the Earth, through language, farming, money, empire and science.

title: A Brief History of Time
author: Stephen Hawking
description: The physicist explains, for readers with no mathematics, what is known about the origin of the universe, black holes and the nature of time.

title: The Selfish Gene
author: Richard Dawkins
description: An argument for looking at evolution from the point of view of the gene, which also introduced the word meme.

title: Silent Spring
author: Rachel Carson
description: A marine biologist documents the harm done by synthetic pesticides to birds, rivers and people, in a book that started the modern environmental movement.

title: Cosmos
author: Carl Sagan
description: A tour of the universe and of how we came to understand it, from the library of Alexandria to the Voyager probes, written alongside the television series.

title: The Immortal Life of Henrietta Lacks
author: Rebecca Skloot
description: Cells taken without consent from a Black tobacco farmer in 1951 became essential to medical research; her family learned of it decades later.

title: Educated
author: Tara Westover
description: Raised by survivalists in the mountains of Idaho with no schooling, Westover teaches herself enough to get into college, and goes on to Cambridge.

title: Becoming
author: Michelle Obama
description: The former First Lady on growing up on the South Side of Chicago, her career as a lawyer, and eight years in the White House.

title: The Diary of a Young Girl
author: Anne Frank
description: The diary a Jewish girl kept for two years while hiding with her family in a secret annex in Amsterdam during the Nazi occupation.

title: I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings
author: Maya Angelou
description: The first volume of Angelou's autobiography, from a childhood in Stamps, Arkansas, through trauma and silence to independence at sixteen.

title: Born a Crime
author: Trevor Noah
description: Growing up in South Africa as the son of a Black mother and a white father, at a time when their relationship was against the law.

title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
author: Daniel Kahneman
description: A psychologist describes the two modes of thought, quick intuition and slow reasoning, and the systematic errors that come from relying on the first.

title: Man's Search for Meaning
author: Viktor E. Frankl
description: A psychiatrist's account of surviving Nazi concentration camps, and the approach to therapy he built on the need to find meaning.

title: Quiet
subtitle: The Power of Introverts in a World That Can't Stop Talking
author: Susan Cain
description: An argument that schools and workplaces built for extroverts undervalue people who think best alone and prefer to listen.

title: Guns, Germs, and Steel
author: Jared Diamond
description: Why did some societies conquer others? Diamond looks to geography, domesticated plants and animals, and disease rather than to the people themselves.

title: The Guns of August
author: Barbara W. Tuchman
description: The first month of the First World War, from the funeral of Edward VII to the Marne, and the plans and mistakes that set its course.

title: The Warmth of Other Suns
author: Isabel Wilkerson
description: The Great Migration of six million Black Americans out of the South, told through three people who left for Chicago, New York and Los Angeles.

title: Freakonomics
author: Steven D. Levitt and Stephen J. Dubner
description: An economist applies the tools of his trade to questions such as cheating teachers, sumo wrestlers and why drug dealers live with their mothers.

title: Capital in the Twenty-First Century
author: Thomas Piketty
description: Using centuries of tax and wealth records, Piketty argues that when returns on capital outpace growth, inequality tends to rise.

title: The Sixth Extinction
subtitle: An Unnatural History
author: Elizabeth Kolbert
description: A journalist visits scientists studying vanishing frogs, corals and bats, and makes the case that humans are causing a mass extinction.

title: Braiding Sweetgrass
author: Robin Wall Kimmerer
description: A botanist and member of the Citizen Potawatomi Nation writes about plants, reciprocity and what scientific and Indigenous knowledge can learn from each other.

title: H Is for Hawk
author: Helen Macdonald
description: After her father's sudden death, Macdonald takes on a goshawk and trains it, while reading the troubled life of the writer T. H. White.

title: Into the Wild
author: Jon Krakauer
description: A young college graduate gives away his savings, travels the American West and walks alone into the Alaskan wilderness; Krakauer pieces together why.

title: In Patagonia
author: Bruce Chatwin
description: A journey to the far south of South America in search of a scrap of animal skin from his childhood, told in short episodes full of stories.

title: A Walk in the Woods
author: Bill Bryson
description: Bryson and an unfit old friend set out to hike the Appalachian Trail, with digressions on its history, ecology and bears.

title: In Cold Blood
author: Truman Capote
description: The 1959 murder of a farming family in Holcomb, Kansas, and the two men who did it, reconstructed from years of interviews.

title: The Devil in the White City
author: Erik Larson
description: The architect who built the 1893 Chicago World's Fair and the killer who used it to find victims, told side by side.

title: Salt, Fat, Acid, Heat
subtitle: Mastering the Elements of Good Cooking
author: Samin Nosrat
description: A cookbook that teaches four principles instead of rules, so you can cook well without a recipe, with illustrations and a hundred recipes to practise on.

title: Mastering the Art of French Cooking
author: Julia Child, Louisette Bertholle and Simone Beck
description: Classic French dishes explained step by step for American home cooks, from omelettes to boeuf bourguignon.

title: Kitchen Confidential
author: Anthony Bourdain
description: A New York chef's account of life behind restaurant kitchen doors, and of his own unruly career in them.

title: Why We Sleep
author: Matthew Walker
description: A sleep researcher explains what sleep and dreams do for memory, health and mood, and what happens when we get too little.

title: Being Mortal
subtitle: Medicine and What Matters in the End
author: Atul Gawande
description: A surgeon on how medicine treats ageing and dying, and how it could ask people what matters to them in the time they have left.

title: Open
subtitle: An Autobiography
author: Andre Agassi
description: The tennis champion writes frankly about a sport he was pushed into as a child and the long road to playing it on his own terms.

title: Moneyball
author: Michael Lewis
description: How the Oakland Athletics, with one of baseball's smallest budgets, used statistics to find players other teams undervalued.

title: Just Kids
author: Patti Smith
description: The musician's memoir of her friendship with the photographer Robert Mapplethorpe in New York in the late 1960s and 1970s.

title: Ways of Seeing
author: John Berger
description: Short essays, some in words and some in pictures, on how oil paintings, photographs and advertisements shape what we see.

title: The Story of Art
author: E. H. Gombrich
description: A single-volume history of art from cave paintings to the twentieth century, written plainly for young readers and read by everyone since.

title: Code
subtitle: The Hidden Language of Computer Hardware and Software
author: Charles Petzold
description: How computers work, built up from Morse code and light bulbs through logic gates and memory to a working processor.

title: The Soul of a New Machine
author: Tracy Kidder
description: A team of engineers at Data General races to design a new minicomputer in a year and a half, told from inside their lab.

title: Mere Christianity
author: C. S. Lewis
description: Adapted from wartime radio talks, Lewis sets out the beliefs he thought Christians of every denomination share.

title: The Fire Next Time
author: James Baldwin
description: Two essays, a letter to Baldwin's nephew and a longer piece on race, religion and America a century after emancipation.

title: Sophie's World
author: Jostein Gaarder
description: A fourteen-year-old in Norway receives letters from a mysterious philosopher, in a novel that is also a history of Western philosophy.

title: James
author: Percival Everett
description: The flight down the Mississippi from Huckleberry Finn, retold by Jim, who is far cleverer than the white people around him are allowed to know.

title: Intermezzo
author: Sally Rooney
description: After their father's death, two very different brothers in Dublin, a lawyer and a chess prodigy, each fall into a complicated love.

title: The Women
author: Kristin Hannah
description: A young nurse volunteers for Vietnam in 1965, and comes home to a country that does not want to hear that women served there too.

title: Orbital
author: Samantha Harvey
description: One day on the International Space Station, sixteen orbits of the Earth, as six astronauts work, remember and watch the planet turn below.

title: Prophet Song
author: Paul Lynch
description: In a Dublin sliding into authoritarian rule, a mother of four tries to hold her family together after her husband is taken by the secret police.

title: North Woods
author: Daniel Mason
description: The history of one house in the woods of western Massachusetts, through the people, animals and ghosts that live there over three centuries.

title: The Covenant of Water
author: Abraham Verghese
description: Three generations of a family in Kerala, from 1900 to the 1970s, haunted by a condition that makes some of them drown.

title: Yellowface
author: R. F. Kuang
description: When a celebrated writer dies, her unsuccessful friend takes her unfinished manuscript and publishes it as her own, and the lies multiply.

title: Fourth Wing
author: Rebecca Yarros
description: Violet Sorrengail is forced to enter a war college for dragon riders, where few cadets survive the year and her mother is the commanding general.

title: Onyx Storm
author: Rebecca Yarros
description: The third book of the Empyrean series: Violet and her friends leave the kingdom's borders in search of allies against the coming enemy.

title: The God of the Woods
author: Liz Moore
description: In 1975 a teenage girl goes missing from a summer camp in the Adirondacks owned by her wealthy family, whose son vanished from the same woods years before.

title: Long Island
author: Colm Tóibín
description: Twenty years after Brooklyn, Eilis Lacey's life on Long Island is upset by a stranger at the door, and she goes home to Ireland for a summer.

title: Martyr!
author: Kaveh Akbar
description: Cyrus Shams, a young Iranian-American poet newly sober in Indiana, becomes obsessed with the idea of a death that means something.

title: The Anxious Generation
author: Jonathan Haidt
description: A social psychologist argues that the move from play-based to phone-based childhood has harmed young people's mental health, and proposes what to do.

title: The Emperor of Gladness
author: Ocean Vuong
description: A nineteen-year-old in a run-down Connecticut town becomes the carer of an elderly widow with dementia, and the two make an odd household.

title: Flesh
author: David Szalay
description: The life of István, from a housing estate in Hungary to the British army and London wealth, told in spare episodes where much is left unsaid.

title: Abundance
author: Ezra Klein and Derek Thompson
description: Two journalists argue that American government has become too slow at building housing, energy and infrastructure, and that it can be fixed.

title: Demon Copperhead
author: Barbara Kingsolver
description: David Copperfield moved to the Appalachian mountains of Virginia: a boy born to a teenage mother makes his way through foster care and the opioid crisis.

title: Tomorrow, and Tomorrow, and Tomorrow
author: Gabrielle Zevin
description: Two friends who met as children over a video game start making games together in college, and spend thirty years as partners and rivals.

title: The Hunger Games
author: Suzanne Collins
description: In the nation of Panem, Katniss Everdeen volunteers in her sister's place for a televised fight to the death between children from each district.

title: Sunrise on the Reaping
author: Suzanne Collins
description: A prequel to The Hunger Games: the fiftieth Games, in which twice as many tributes are reaped, seen through a sixteen-year-old from District 12.

title: The Hate U Give
author: Angie Thomas
description: Starr Carter moves between her poor neighbourhood and her suburban prep school, until she witnesses a police officer shoot her unarmed friend.

title: Speak
author: Laurie Halse Anderson
description: Melinda starts high school as an outcast after calling the police at a party, and over a year finds a way to say what happened to her there.

title: The Fault in Our Stars
author: John Green
description: Two teenagers who meet at a cancer support group fall in love and travel to Amsterdam to find the author of their favourite novel.

title: The Perks of Being a Wallflower
author: Stephen Chbosky
description: In letters to an unnamed friend, a shy boy describes his first year of high school, the older friends who take him in, and what he has been avoiding.

title: The Outsiders
author: S. E. Hinton
description: Ponyboy Curtis and his brothers belong to the greasers, poor kids in an Oklahoma town always at odds with the rich socs across town.

title: The Giver
author: Lois Lowry
description: In a community without pain or choice, twelve-year-old Jonas is chosen to receive its memories of the past from the one old man who keeps them.

title: Six of Crows
author: Leigh Bardugo
description: A teenage criminal mastermind assembles a crew of six outcasts for an impossible heist on the most secure fortress in the world.

title: The Book Thief
author: Markus Zusak
description: Narrated by Death: a girl in a small town in Nazi Germany steals books, learns to read, and shares them with the Jewish man hidden in her basement.

title: Eleanor & Park
author: Rainbow Rowell
description: Omaha, 1986: two misfit sixteen-year-olds who share a bus seat fall in love over comic books and mixtapes.

title: Aristotle and Dante Discover the Secrets of the Universe
author: Benjamin Alire Sáenz
description: Two Mexican-American boys in 1980s El Paso meet at a swimming pool and become friends, then something more.

title: Children of Blood and Bone
author: Tomi Adeyemi
description: In a West African-inspired kingdom where magic has been taken away, Zélie sets out with a runaway princess to bring it back.

title: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
author: Holly Jackson
description: For a school project, Pippa reinvestigates a five-year-old murder case in her English town, convinced the accused boy did not do it.

title: The Poet X
author: Elizabeth Acevedo
description: A novel in verse: Xiomara, growing up in Harlem with a strict religious mother, fills a notebook with poems and joins a slam poetry club.

title: Long Way Down
author: Jason Reynolds
description: Will's brother has been shot, and he takes the gun to settle it; on the elevator ride down, seven people from his past get on.

title: American Born Chinese
author: Gene Luen Yang
description: Three stories in comics, about the Monkey King, a Chinese-American boy at a new school, and an unbearable cousin, that turn out to be one.

title: Heartstopper: Volume 1
author: Alice Oseman
description: Charlie, a shy boy at an English grammar school, is seated next to Nick, a cheerful rugby player, and they become friends, then more.

title: A Wizard of Earthsea
author: Ursula K. Le Guin
description: A gifted, proud boy from a goatherding island goes to the school for wizards, and in showing off lets loose a shadow that hunts him.

title: Where the Wild Things Are
author: Maurice Sendak
description: Sent to bed without supper, Max sails off to an island of wild things, who make him their king, until he wants to be where someone loves him best.

title: The Very Hungry Caterpillar
author: Eric Carle
description: A caterpillar eats through a week of foods, one more each day, with holes in the pages, before spinning a cocoon.

title: Goodnight Moon
author: Margaret Wise Brown
description: A young rabbit says goodnight to everything in the great green room, one quiet page at a time.

title: The Cat in the Hat
author: Dr. Seuss
description: Two children stuck indoors on a rainy day get a visit from a cat who brings chaos, and a fish who objects to all of it.

title: The Snowy Day
author: Ezra Jack Keats
description: Peter wakes to snow in the city and spends the day making tracks, angels and a snowball he tries to keep in his pocket.

title: The Gruffalo
author: Julia Donaldson
description: A mouse walking through the woods invents a fearsome monster to scare off the animals that want to eat him, and then meets it.

title: The Tale of Peter Rabbit
author: Beatrix Potter
description: Disobeying his mother, Peter squeezes into Mr McGregor's garden, eats too many vegetables and only just escapes without his jacket.

title: Charlotte's Web
author: E. B. White
description: Wilbur the pig is saved from the butcher by a spider in the barn who writes words about him in her web.

title: Matilda
author: Roald Dahl
description: A brilliant girl with awful parents and a monstrous headmistress discovers she can move things with her mind, and puts it to good use.

title: Charlie and the Chocolate Factory
author: Roald Dahl
description: Charlie Bucket finds a golden ticket and joins four badly behaved children on a tour of Willy Wonka's extraordinary factory.

title: Holes
author: Louis Sachar
description: Wrongly sent to a desert detention camp, Stanley Yelnats digs a hole every day, and begins to wonder what the warden is really looking for.

title: Wonder
author: R. J. Palacio
description: Auggie Pullman, born with a facial difference, goes to school for the first time in fifth grade, told by him and by those around him.

title: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
author: J. K. Rowling
description: On his eleventh birthday an unwanted orphan learns he is a wizard, and leaves his aunt and uncle for Hogwarts School.

title: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe
author: C. S. Lewis
description: Four children evacuated from London find a wardrobe that leads to Narnia, held in endless winter by the White Witch.

title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland
author: Lewis Carroll
description: Alice follows a white rabbit down a hole into a world of shrinking and growing, mad tea parties and a queen who wants heads off.

title: Winnie-the-Pooh
author: A. A. Milne
description: Stories of a bear of very little brain and his friends in the Hundred Acre Wood, told to Christopher Robin.

title: Diary of a Wimpy Kid
author: Jeff Kinney
description: Greg Heffley keeps a journal, with cartoons, of his first year of middle school and his schemes to become popular.

title: The Hobbit
author: J. R. R. Tolkien
description: Bilbo Baggins, who likes his home and his meals, is talked into joining thirteen dwarves on a journey to take back their treasure from a dragon.

title: Le Petit Prince
author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
description: A pilot stranded in the Sahara meets a small prince from an asteroid, who tells him about his rose and the grown-ups he met on his travels.

title: Hatchet
author: Gary Paulsen
description: After a plane crash in the Canadian wilderness, thirteen-year-old Brian has only a hatchet and his wits to survive until rescue.

title: Bridge to Terabithia
author: Katherine Paterson
description: Jess and his new neighbour Leslie invent a secret kingdom in the woods across a creek, reached by a rope swing.

title: Dog Man
author: Dav Pilkey
description: A police officer and his dog are joined into one crime-fighting hero, Dog Man, who chases a cat called Petey through a series of silly comics.

title: The Wild Robot
author: Peter Brown
description: A robot washed up on a remote island learns from the animals how to survive there, and becomes mother to an orphaned gosling.

title: Casablanca
author: Michael Curtiz
description: In wartime Morocco, an American club owner is asked to help the woman who left him escape with her husband, a Resistance leader.

title: The Godfather
author: Francis Ford Coppola
description: The ageing head of a New York crime family hands control to his youngest son, who had wanted no part of the business.

title: Some Like It Hot
author: Billy Wilder
description: Two musicians who witness a gangland killing in Chicago escape by joining an all-women band headed for Florida, in disguise.

title: 七人の侍
subtitle: Seven Samurai
author: Akira Kurosawa
description: A poor farming village hires seven masterless samurai to defend it from bandits who will return at harvest.

title: 千と千尋の神隠し
subtitle: Spirited Away
author: Hayao Miyazaki
description: Ten-year-old Chihiro is trapped in a bathhouse for spirits after her parents are turned into pigs, and must work there to free them.

title: となりのトトロ
subtitle: My Neighbor Totoro
author: Hayao Miyazaki
description: Two sisters move to the country to be near their sick mother and meet the large, gentle forest spirit who lives nearby.

title: 기생충
subtitle: Parasite
author: Bong Joon-ho
description: A poor family in Seoul gets itself hired, one member at a time, by a wealthy household, until a discovery in the basement changes everything.

title: Le Fabuleux Destin d'Amélie Poulain
subtitle: Amélie
author: Jean-Pierre Jeunet
description: A shy waitress in Montmartre decides to quietly improve the lives of the people around her, while avoiding her own.

title: El laberinto del fauno
subtitle: Pan's Labyrinth
author: Guillermo del Toro
description: In Spain in 1944, a girl living with her cruel stepfather, an army captain, is set three tasks by a faun in an old labyrinth.

title: La Marche de l'empereur
subtitle: March of the Penguins
author: Luc Jacquet
description: A documentary following emperor penguins across the Antarctic winter as they walk inland to breed and raise their chicks.

title: Free Solo
author: Elizabeth Chai Vasarhelyi and Jimmy Chin
description: A documentary about Alex Honnold's attempt to climb the 900-metre face of El Capitan in Yosemite without ropes.

title: Hidden Figures
author: Theodore Melfi
description: Three Black women mathematicians at NASA in the early 1960s do the calculations behind John Glenn's orbit of the Earth.

title: Paddington
author: Paul King
description: A polite young bear from Peru arrives in London looking for a home and is taken in by the Brown family, to Mr Brown's alarm.

title: Toy Story
author: John Lasseter
description: A pull-string cowboy who is a boy's favourite toy feels threatened when a space ranger action figure arrives for his birthday.
